entries.note:
Stop targets descendants from a fresh numeric process-tree snapshot, then the owned root. Windows uses taskkill /T. POSIX escalates after a grace period only while the tracked PTY remains alive. Adversarial detached descendants and PID-reuse edge cases still need qualification; do not claim this is a security sandbox.

Moved here from `orchestrator/server/sessions.mjs` when F178 deleted it: the walk is the same one, reading the same `ps` table and never `pgrep`, and `stop` still sends TERM to the descendants before the root, waits its 2 s, then sends KILL. The JS `Sessions.stop` that used to do this now asks this function through the service and applies the snapshot it answers with.
